name: Alternating Dumbbell Curl
summary: A standing isolation exercise that curls one dumbbell at a time with forearm supination to target the biceps.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with arms fully extended and palms facing your torso in a neutral grip.
Brace your core, retract your shoulder blades slightly, and look straight ahead.
steps: Keeping your upper arm pinned to your side, curl one dumbbell upward.
As the dumbbell passes your hip, rotate your forearm so your palm faces upward by the peak of the curl.
Squeeze your bicep firmly at the top without letting your elbow drift forward.
Lower the dumbbell under control back to the starting neutral position.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm to complete one alternating pair.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you curl the weight upward and inhale smoothly as you lower it back down.
cues: Keep elbows locked at your ribs
Turn the pinky up at the top

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso or using hip momentum to initiate the curl.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the dumbbell weight and keep your core braced to maintain a strict, upright torso.

common_faults.fault: Elbows drifting forward during the upward phase.
common_faults.correction: Keep your upper arms stationary and perpendicular to the floor to prevent the front deltoids from taking over.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the bottom range of motion short.
common_faults.correction: Fully extend the elbow at the bottom of each rep to stretch the biceps under load before initiating the next curl.

precautions: Avoid hyperextending the lower back when handling heavier dumbbells.
